message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 22 November 2026, 23:40 UTC to 23 November 2026, 23:40 UTC (24 November, 05:10 IST). **Scope:** Products.txt only, normalized and deduplicated, plus the required MongoDB ecosystem sweep.

One relevant new status update was identified for an existing critical vulnerability. The vulnerability itself was disclosed before this window.

**OpenJDK / Ubuntu and OpenSearch: CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell)**  
**Severity:** Critical according to Red Hat. Malformed Base64 input can trigger memory corruption and potentially arbitrary code execution in affected OpenJDK configurations on certain x86-64 processors. On 23 November, Ubuntu published its package-status update, including that OpenJDK 26 on Ubuntu 26.04 is affected and will not receive further updates; Scalingo also reported availability of a patched OpenJDK for its OpenSearch 2.19.7-1 service. OpenJDK, Ubuntu, and OpenSearch are on the monitored list; impact depends on the Java build, processor and deployment. Review the applicable vendor guidance and installed versions. [Ubuntu status update](https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/java4shell-cve-2026-114938-status-in-supported-ubuntu-releases/92318); [Red Hat advisory](https://access.redhat.com/security/vulnerabilities/RHSB-2026-018); [Scalingo bulletin](https://doc.scalingo.com/security/bulletins/ssb-2026-008).

**MongoDB ecosystem:** The sweep included searches for Server and its editions, mongod/mongos, Atlas services, management tools, Compass, mongosh, database tools, Kubernetes operators, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, and official integrations and libraries, including vendor-owned advisories without MongoDB in their titles. On 23 November [CERT-FR issued a driver advisory](https://cert.cyber.gouv.fr/avis/CERTFR-2026-AVI-1606/), referencing MongoDB bulletins from 19 November. These are earlier disclosures, not newly disclosed vulnerabilities; the advisory is worth checking against deployed drivers. The advisory does not assign an overall severity.

**Closing:** Prompt review of the OpenJDK update is recommended for applicable deployments. Search indexing and incomplete publication timestamps limit coverage; absence of other findings is not proof that no other vulnerabilities exist. Continue addressing earlier disclosures.
